name: Katukína-Kanamarí
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (0 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, final stress, suffixes stressless so stress stays word-final) rests on the standard 448-pp reference grammar (dos Anjos 2011, LOT/VU), whose sec. 2.7 I re-read in the recovered cached PDF: the quotation is there at pp.108-111 with instrumental pitch/intensity figures backing it. The record's held list was empty and grade/loc fields blank; the file is now on the backup volume, so the record can carry a page locator (pp.104-111) and a top strength of the evidence. The independent second grammar (Ishy de Magalhães 2018, Unicamp, downloaded now) states the same fixed final primary stress for Juruá Kanamari and adds (i) secondary stress on the second syllable to the left of the tonic (iterative iambs R-to-L in her 2012 MA) and (ii) a small set of derived words where adjectivizer -nin is unstressed and stress stays on the root (penult surface stress). Neither changes 'fixed-domi

sources.citation: dos Anjos 2011, Fonologia e Gramatica Katukina-Kanamari, sec. 2.7 Acento (full text, cached copy)
sources.quote: A constancia da altura e sempre na ultima silaba dos vocabulos ... os sufixos sao desprovidos de acento proprio, seu acrescimo ... faz com que o acento do vocabulo fique na ultima silaba da palavra fonologica ... Consideramos, entao, que o acento e previsivel na lingua.

sources.citation: Ishy de Magalhães, Priscila Hanako. 2018. Kanamari do Juruá (família Katukina): aspectos fonológicos e morfossintáticos. Tese de doutorado, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (412 pp).
sources.quote: 'pode-se classificar o acento na língua Kanamari como previsível, pois, ocorre em posição fixa na última sílaba' (p.81); compounds stress the last syllable of the last morpheme; 'O acento secundário ocorre sempre na segunda sílaba à esquerda da sílaba mais proeminente' (p.82); in 'algumas palavras derivadas' with adjectivizer -nin the affix is stressless and stress stays on the root, giving paroxytones (exx. 110-115, p.83-84); vowel length is contrastive and not a stress correlate; long vowels do not occur in stressed syllables except monosyllables (p.85).
sources.locator: sec. 2.5 O acento, pp.81-86 (2.5.1 Acento morfológico p.83; 2.5.3 Duração e acento pp.85-86)
sources.note: Second full grammar (different dialect area, Juruá); adds the secondary-stress rule (alternating, two syllables left of the final main stress) and the stressless -nin adjectivizer exceptions that our record's the secondary-stress rule/exception fields lack.
sources.venue: Tese de doutorado, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (412 pp)

sources.citation: dos Anjos, Zoraide. 2011. Fonologia e Gramática Katukina-Kanamari. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Utrecht: LOT (448 pp). [recovered from session cache of, VU Research Portal publisher's PDF]
sources.quote: Pitch and intensity coincide on the last syllable; pitch is constant on the final syllable even when intensity is not; suffixes lack their own stress so suffixation leaves stress on the last syllable of the phonological word; stress is predictable. In fast speech a phonological phrase may carry a single stress on its last syllable (Regra 2). Compounds: one stress on the last syllable (p.215).
sources.locator: sec. 2.7 Acento, pp.104-111; sec. 2.8 Frase fonológica pp.111-113; p.215 (compounds)

sources.citation: Ishy de Magalhães, Priscila Hanako. 2012. Uma análise fonológica da língua kanamari (Katukina). Dissertação de mestrado, Universidade de Brasília (175 pp).
sources.quote: Stress predictable, 'na maioria das vezes, ocorre na última sílaba'; secondary stress on the second syllable to the left of the main stress; metrical analysis: binary right-headed feet built iteratively right-to-left, degenerate feet allowed (exx. 248-250); some affixes (e.g. -niN) extrametrical so stress stays on the root; analysis called preliminary.
sources.note: Dedicated phonology with a Hayes-style metrical analysis (iambic R-to-L feet) usable for the rhythm/secondary-stress coding; superseded in substance by the 2018 thesis.
sources.venue: Dissertação de mestrado, Universidade de Brasília (175 pp)

sources.citation: Queixalós, Francesc and dos Anjos G.S., Zoraide (2006). A língua Katukína-Kanamarí. LIAMES 6. pp. 29-60.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: A grande maioria das palavras se encaixa no padrão oxítono: i'tSun 'arco', w¨:'l¨ 'garganta', mana'ti 'noite', woi'kan 'remar', ma:pi'kan 'escutar', wapika'l¨ 'boto'. O acréscimo de sufixos leva o acento a se deslocar para o fim da palavra: ki'taN 'dormir', kitaN-'niN 'dormindo'. Esse fenômeno parece não acontecer em todos os casos. O estudo sistemático da colocação do acento em função da concatenação dos morfemas está ainda por se fazer. [...] O correlato fonético do acento é a altura do tom fundamental (para ilustrações acústicas, cf. Dos Anjos 2005b).
sources.locator: Sec. 5.3 Acento, printed p. 37; Sec. 5.4.3 Acento, printed p. 39
sources.note: Final (oxytone) stress, one stress marked per word, matching the catalog final stress. Adds: suffixation moves stress to the word end (kitaN-'niN), hedged as apparently not holding in all cases, with the systematic study of stress placement under morpheme concatenation left for future work; phonetic correlate of stress is F0 height. No secondary stress, weight, or domain statement; lexical tone not mentioned (consistent with catalog tone_cls not-mentioned). The stress section does not say which dialect (Biá Katukína or Itaquaí Kanamarí) the examples come from; the article covers both

sources.note: The ELDP/ELAR project abstract states the project 'will provide a phonetic description and a phonological analysis of the language, necessary for an adequate orthography' together with an annotated audio/video corpus and a Kanamari-Portuguese-English dictionary; whether the deposited phonology write-up (if any) discusses pitch/tone is unknown. Given the known descriptions (fixed final stress, pitch as a stress correlate), any statement would most likely be 'no lexical tone'.
